ms.report:
Dear reviewers, I'm happy to submit the Proof of Achievement for Milestone 1.
While the goal for the first milestone was to provide a working but incomplete version of the plugin, I decided to put extra effort and already implemented all of the available NMKR API endpoints, because a lot of time will be required to fully debug the code, creating the test framework planned for Milestone 2, and, most importantly, develop the example game that is planned for Milestones 3 and 4.
The code available in the official Github repository contains the minimal example application mentioned in the Acceptance criteria, documentation is available directly in the Godot game engine, and the README.md file is updated with code examples, setup instructions, and a list of all the available endpoints divided by category.
To show the output of my work, I recorded a video that goes through all the points mentioned in the Milestone Outputs, so that you don't have to install the Godot game engine and define an NMKR API key just to check if the code works.

Links:
Official repository: https://github.com/Odiobill/NmkrGodot
Recorded video: https://youtu.be/zYt-qpAeA-0

Dear reviewers, thank you very much for the remarks about the previous submission.
Indeed, the video link was missing in the README.md files, and I added it: it's the same video I recorded for the previous Milestone, which also shows how to set up the plugin.
Regarding the bug-fixing, luckily the code was pretty robust and the only required changes were due to different return types that some of the NMKR API endpoints provide. ・Commit 3cb0c86

Dear Reviewers, I’m resubmitting the PoA for Milestone 3 after the request of a Catalyst Reviewer, who asked to remove any reference to the Close-out video and report, which should be included only in the final milestone.
Since the same PoA was already approved before, I just removed those references and instead added a short, different video to show the implementation of the features required in this milestone, while leaving all the rest as it was before.

Due to issues that emerged while trying to work with the previously selected graphics artists, assigned to deliver both the graphics required for the example game and its NFT collection, until recent times, it was not possible to deliver two of the required acceptance criteria, because there was the need to create the above-mentioned NFT collection.
Fortunately, this did not affect other parts of the project, needed in the Final Milestone, and I was able to complete all the requirements for both the remaining milestones shortly after the new graphic artist delivered the necessary assets.
Milestone 3 required two outputs:
Output 1: Release of the first, incomplete alpha version of the example game
The defined Acceptance Criteria required the release of an incomplete version of the game, which implemented the following Web3-related tasks:
・Minting a custom NFT from a new policy ID, created for this game
・Wallet ownership verification
・Selection of the game assets from the wallet

The example game source code, with all the available art, is hosted in a dedicated repository, available at https://github.com/Odiobill/YASG

ms.report:
Dear Catalyst reviewers, I’m happy to submit the Proof of Achievements for the Final Milestone. As kindly requested, I'm now providing the Close-out Report in PDF format for archiving purposes.

The required outputs were the following:
1 - Release of the full version of the example game. It will be a "snake clone" but with different features compared to the original one.
As per the submitted "Acceptance criteria" and "Evidence of milestone completion", it should be possible to build the game for multiple platforms: it should be available for at least 3 of the following: Linux, Mac, Windows, and Web. As mentioned in the Proof of Achievement for Milestone 3, the example game for the NMKR SDK for Godot has been released and it is available for Linux, Windows, and Web.
Builds for Linux and Windows are available as “releases” in the GitHub repository: https://github.com/Odiobill/YASG/releases 
A web version is playable at the following address: https://rookiez.org/yasg/
It was also required that depending on the player's assets, there will be different graphics and features (like speed or "resistance") for the snake controlled by the player: the player is allowed to choose which assets to use for the game, and it's possible to use either one of the custom NFTs or already existing tokens: $SNEK and $VIPER.
Depending on the selected asset, the look of the snake will change, and it will have different characteristics: several skills can be improved depending on the metadata stored with the NFTs. The game's main menu shows a recap of the skills for each asset, rated in stars for Agility, Efficiency, and Resistance.
You can check the Close-out Video for a visual representation of those features: https://youtu.be/bcVj_lub2UM 
2 - All the found bugs in the "NMKR SDK for Godot" plugin are fixed
